hints.title: Customer Order Types
hints.text: Determine which customers have placed at least one order of type zero.

hints.title: Conditional Order Inclusion
hints.text: Always include type zero orders in the output table.

hints.title: Exclude Type One for Identified Customers
hints.text: Include type one orders only when the placing customer has no recorded type zero transactions.

hints.title: Complete Query
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT order_id, customer_id, order_type
FROM Orders
WHERE order_type = 0
   OR customer_id NOT IN (
       SELECT DISTINCT customer_id
       FROM Orders
       WHERE order_type = 0
   );
```

complexity.space: O(C) distinct customers with type 0 orders
complexity.notes: Preserves type 0 orders unconditionally and retains type 1 only if customer never ordered type 0.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simple grouping drops individual order detail attributes.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Anti-join subquery or window MIN check maintains all order rows without joins.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should use NOT IN or window MIN partition to check customer order profile.

solutions.approach: Filter orders using OR condition with NOT IN subquery identifying customers having type 0 orders.

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def drop_specific_orders(orders: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    has_zero = set(orders[orders['order_type'] == 0]['customer_id'])
    cond = (orders['order_type'] == 0) | (~orders['customer_id'].isin(has_zero))
    return orders[cond][['order_id', 'customer_id', 'order_type']]
solutions.approach: Identify customer IDs having order_type == 0 and filter rows that are type 0 or not in that set.
